title: Loss of consortium claims - an underused head of compensation
p1:
A serious injury does not only affect the person who is hurt.

Sometimes, the biggest changes happen quietly at home — in relationships, support, and everyday life.
p2:
Many people assume compensation only covers medical bills, lost income, or physical pain. But some legal systems also recognize loss of consortium claims, which address the impact an injury can have on a spouse’s or family relationship.

The surprising part? Many eligible people never explore this type of claim because they do not realize it exists.
p3:
Loss of consortium can relate to the loss of companionship, affection, assistance, or the normal benefits of a close relationship after an injury. It is not about putting a price on a relationship; it recognizes that serious harm can affect more than one person.

A useful takeaway: when assessing the full impact of an injury, look beyond the obvious costs. The personal and family consequences may also matter.
conclusion: Have you come across a situation where the impact of an injury on family life was overlooked during a compensation discussion?
